old: A 1934 10 centavos coin from Guatemala. One side shows the coat of arms - a quetzal, crossed rifles and swords, and laurel - with the words REPUBLICA DE GUATEMALA, the fineness 0.720 and the year 1934. The other side shows a quetzal perched on a column, with the words LEY DE 26 DE NOVIEMBRE DE 1924, 10 and CENTAVOS. Struck in silver, .720 fine.

old: A 1964 20 centavos coin from Mexico. The obverse shows the national arms. Struck in brass (95% copper, 5% zinc).

old: A 1962 20 centavos coin from Cuba. The reverse shows a portrait of José Martí with the date. The arms side shows the words REPUBLICA DE CUBA and the national shield (the Escudo - a key, stripes and a palm), with oak and laurel branches and a star on a Phrygian cap, and the words VEINTE CENTAVOS. Struck in copper-nickel.
